verdict: O'Reilly grew sales 9% on strong same-store sales, and kept about 15 cents of every sales dollar as profit.

segments.name: Auto parts sales
segments.note: Parts, batteries, tools and supplies sold to DIY customers and professional installers through O'Reilly stores and online — the company reports a single segment.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Store payroll, rent and running the store network — O'Reilly's only operating-expense line.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $82M, partly offset by $2M of interest income and $4M of other income — a net $76M cost.

takeaways.title: Existing stores did the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: Comparable store sales rose 7.2% — growth came from selling more through stores O'Reilly already has, not just from opening new ones.

takeaways.title: EPS grew 14%, faster than sales
takeaways.text: Diluted EPS rose 14% to $0.97. Buybacks helped: O'Reilly repurchased $1.03B of its own stock in the quarter alone.

takeaways.title: More than half of each sale survives the parts bill
takeaways.text: Gross margin was 52.4% of sales (gross profit $2.68B) — the markup on parts funds the stores and still leaves a 21.4% operating margin.

footerNote: O'Reilly reports one operating segment, so revenue is a single line. Figures are rounded to $M.
follow100Note: Management raised full-year 2026 guidance during the quarter, including comparable store sales of +5.5% to +6.5% and revenue of $19.0B to $19.3B.
